identificationModule.briefTitle: Metflex: The Effectiveness of a Dietary Intervention
identificationModule.officialTitle: Employing Dynamic Kinetic Responses to Demonstrate the Effectiveness of Dietary Intervention: A Challenge-based Study Using a Low-glycaemic Load Diet

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
This study is testing the effectiveness of a dietary intervention by means of measuring the change in RQ upon a hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp challenge and by means of measuring the kinetic responses of multiple PF markers (including RQ) to an acute mixed meal challenge before and after a 6-week dietary intervention. The challenges will be applied to investigate whether the kinetic response is a better measure for health and wellbeing when compared to fasting (baseline) levels. In addition, several measures that reflect perceivable benefits like mood, quality of life, sleep quality, cognitive and physical performance will be assessed in a first exploratory attempt to link (changes in) PF to consumer perceivable benefits.

Subjects will be randomly allocated to a low glycemic load diet or a 'Western' diet for 6 weeks. Before and after the intervention several measurements will take place. The low glycemic load diet will be high in polyphenols, protein, vegetables, pulses, fibres and nuts, and low in glycemic carbohydrates. All these dietary factors have been shown to improve glycemic control and/or to reduce metabolic syndrome risk factors.

armGroups.label: Low glycaemic load diet
armGroups.description: Subjects will be following a low glycaemic load diet, typically high in polyphenols, proteins, vegetables, pulses, fibres and nuts, and low in glycemic carbohydrates, for six continuous weeks.

armGroups.label: Western diet
armGroups.description: Subjects will be following a western diet, typically high in saturated fat, refined sugars and salt, and low in fruit and vegetables and fibers, for six continuous weeks.

interventions.name: Low glycaemic load diet
interventions.description: Subjects will first be subjected to a 2-week run-in diet consisting of products that fit into a typical 'Western' diet. Thereafter subjects will be allocated to a low glycemic load diet for 6 weeks.

interventions.name: Western diet
interventions.description: Subjects will first be subjected to a 2-week run-in diet consisting of products that fit into a typical 'Western' diet. Thereafter subjects will be allocated to a 'Western' diet for 6 weeks.

primaryOutcomes.measure: Metabolic flexibility, as measured by delta RQ (change in RQ) upon a hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Metabolic flexibility, as measured by delta RQ (change in RQ) upon a mixed meal challenge
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Phenotypic flexibility markers, as measured by various blood parameters such as lipids, glucose, inflammatory markers and more, upon a mixed meal challenge
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Diet-induced changes in the Kinetic responses vs. the baseline values of RQ and various phenotypic flexibility parameters such as lipids, glucose, inflammatory markers and more
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Phenotypic flexibility markers, as measured by various blood parameters such as lipids, glucose, inflammatory markers and more, in the fasted state
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Insulin sensitivity, as measured by a hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Functional markers of cognitive performance, as measured by attention, memory and executive function
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Functional markers of physical performance, as measured by the timed up-and-go test (TUGT), the 6-minute walk test, handgrip and muscle strength tests
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Sleep quality, as assessed with the10-item Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Mood, as assessed by the Affect grid
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Quality of life, as assessed by a 32-item questionnaire, including social, spiritual, emotional, cognitive, physical, activities of daily living and integrated quality of life
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: Body composition, as measured by the deuterium water method
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: Within 5 days before the start of the 6 week dietary intervention and again in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: 36-hour blood pressure, as measured by the continuous blood pressure device mobil-o-graph
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: 36 hours within 5 days before the 6 week dietary intervention and again 36 hours in the 6th week of the dietary intervention

otherOutcomes.measure: 36-hour glycaemic response, as measured by the continuous blood glucose device ipro2 (Medtronic)
otherOutcomes.timeFrame: 36 hours within 5 days before the 6 week dietary intervention and again 36 hours in the 6th week of the dietary intervention
